claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me the **name and date of birth of each child** you'd like me to assess for eligibility?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'd like to check if I can claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He just turned 19 a few months ago, so I want to make sure I'm still eligible.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I appreciate you providing that context.

So your son is **Alex** and he's now **19 years old**. Just to confirm the details and ensure I have the right information:

**What is Alex's exact date of birth?**

This will help me determine his eligibility status accurately.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, let me think... he was born on March 15th, 2006. So yes, he's just turned 19 this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So Alex was born on 15th March 2006 and has just turned 19.

Before I can make a final determination, I need to understand your family situation a bit better. Let me ask:

**Is Alex in full-time education or approved training?**

This is an important factor that could affect his eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education - he's doing his A-levels at sixth form college. He's planning to finish them this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know, thank you. So Alex is currently in full-time education doing his A-levels.

Just to clarify one more thing:

**Is Alex living with you, or is he living away from home (for example, in halls of residence or with another relative)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives at home with me, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have one final question to complete my assessment:

**Are you a British citizen or do you have the right to reside in the UK?** (This includes having settled status, visa permission, or other qualifying immigration status.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have all the details I need to make my assessment.

Based on the information you've provided, let me determine Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit:

- Alex was born on 15th March 2006, making him 19 years old
- He is in full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- He lives with you at home
- You are a UK resident

Under Child Benefit rules, children can continue to be eligible beyond age 16 if they are in full-time education or approved training, up until the end of the month in which they turn 19. Since Alex is currently 19 and still in full-time education completing his A-levels, he should remain eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. 

Since he's currently in full-time education and hasn't yet turned 20, he qualifies as a dependent child. This eligibility will continue as long as he remains in full-time education. You should be aware that once he finishes his A-levels and stops full-time education, his eligibility will end.

If you have any other questions or need further assistance, please let me know!
